title: The Primary Objective, Priced

source.title: Netanyahu promises Iran regime change: Can Israel topple Tehran government?
source.note: AJ's own explainer (the cuttable form, per the roster) — not a wire. Non-US horizon, flagged. Read in full via the cloud fetch; reductions filed, no quotation over fifteen words

object.label: the next offensive against Iran — the force (slate01) · the war that made the crunch (PG01 §5); the Strait touched at ¶18 and ¶24

zAxis.pos: renewed strikes come, with Washington in them, and the government falls
zAxis.neg: they do not — no US, no ground, no fall

transformNote: Netanyahu's 'primary objective' (regime change) asserted thirty years running — 1996 to Congress, March 2026 ('a ground component'), this week with his own election seven days out. The page prices it: airpower degrades, does not topple; no ground force exists (the Kurds were weighed in March and dropped); Washington has not signed (the FT: an Israeli proposal for renewed strikes refused — on timing). The NYT's 10-21 report (US–Israeli plans for strikes after the midterms) is the same object from the other side; nytimes.com is blocked from the cut's fetch and NPR's digest of it is robots-blocked, so this is the day's only full read on the object

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: Netanyahu promises Iran regime change: can Israel topple Tehran's government?
lines.note: THE DOOR: a promise and a question — the headline carries its own doubt. 'Promises' is the frame; the question is the cut's
lines.zWhy: a promise the headline questions is read as not yet

lines.quote: toppling Iran's government remains Israel's 'primary objective', as his poll support declines before national elections next week
lines.note: the aim restated against a second clock — Israel's election, seven days out — beside the US one (11-03). Two principals, two votes, one object
lines.zWhy: an objective restated a week before an election leans toward the next strike

lines.quote: after calls with Trump on Sunday and Hegseth's visit, no sign Washington agreed to join another offensive, let alone removal of the leadership
lines.note: THE GAP: the partner has not signed. Dated (Sunday 10-18); the visit is the record
lines.zWhy: no sign of Washington is no next offensive with Washington in it

lines.quote: analysts: Israel has the firepower to do serious damage but no clear plan to turn gains into the government's fall; a ground invasion would take far more
lines.note: the page's thesis, attributed in the plural; the instrument named (ground) and its absence
lines.zWhy: firepower without a plan for the fall is damage, not change

lines.quote: a state that survived two rounds and can still retaliate against Israel and the Gulf neighbours hosting US assets; Washington has found no credible way to force its terms
lines.note: the Gulf hosts are the arc's own ground — Bahrain's base, priced at $400M on 10-21 (msnow). 'No credible way' is the page's reading of the US position
lines.zWhy: a state that survived twice and can still hit the hosts is not falling on the third

lines.quote: Israel could again establish air superiority and strike Iranian targets — offensive stockpiles and aerial refuelling
lines.note: capability conceded by the analyst; the one line on the page that leans toward the strike
lines.zWhy: air superiority available is a strike available

lines.quote: the most dangerous of these regimes is Iran — a cruel despotism wed to a fanatic militancy
lines.note: constitutive — the principal to Congress, July 1996. As-of date 1996: thirty years of the same object. Never Dia-scored

lines.quote: the June 2025 war and the campaign launched on February 28 gave him the intervention he sought; the government did not fall
lines.note: THE RECORD: two rounds, both dated, one outcome. The object's own history on the page
lines.zWhy: two rounds without a fall read against a third producing one

lines.quote: you can't do it only from the air — there has to be a ground component
lines.note: constitutive — the principal, March 2026. His own falsifier: no ground, no fall. The page then shows there is no ground

lines.quote: airpower can degrade military capabilities but cannot fully destroy them; well-hidden systems would survive
lines.note: the instrument's limit stated as a rule
lines.zWhy: what airpower cannot destroy is what survives the next strike

lines.quote: overthrow would require deploying troops and staying for years; the covert methods of earlier attacks cannot be assumed to work again
lines.note: the ground component priced in years; the covert route discounted
lines.zWhy: troops for years that no one has committed is no fall

lines.quote: human intelligence assets on the ground and cyberattacks could feature, but using them burns them — a concrete military gain becomes the test
lines.note: 'use and burn': the covert instrument priced by what it costs to spend
lines.zWhy: assets that burn when used are a one-time strike, not a campaign

lines.quote: CNN, citing Kurdish and US officials: arming Kurdish opposition groups was discussed in March and never advanced — they lacked the capability against the IRGC
lines.note: the only ground force weighed, dated (March), dropped, attributed. The lowest-Dia line on the page
lines.zWhy: the one proxy ground force considered and dropped is no ground force

lines.quote: Iran likely still holds sizeable missile stocks, even if damage to targeting systems limits their effect
lines.note: the retaliation layer, sized as 'sizeable' — the analyst's honest vagueness
lines.zWhy: a stock that survives is a cost the next strike pays

lines.quote: antiship missile stockpiles probably remain large — easy to produce, older Chinese designs brought in-house, the southern mountains for shelter
lines.note: THE STRAIT'S LAYER: the antiship stock is what prices passage (H6 — who sets the price of the Strait). Marked: this line reads H6, not the declared object
lines.zWhy: a large antiship stock is a strait still priced by Iran

lines.quote: Israel's interceptor stocks were depleted by previous exchanges; expensive interceptors against cheap drones strain supply in a long exchange
lines.note: the exchange rate of the war — interceptor against drone — stated as the constraint on duration
lines.zWhy: depleted interceptors make a long campaign the costlier side's

lines.quote: US participation unlikely: diverging interests between Tel Aviv and Washington; Trump under pressure to avoid renewed escalation before the midterms
lines.note: THE CLOCK: the US election as the brake, in the page's own reading. The NYT's 10-21 plans are for after it
lines.zWhy: a partner braking until the election is no offensive before it

lines.quote: the Financial Times: an Israeli proposal for renewed strikes failed to win Trump's approval — a disagreement over immediate action, not a permanent rejection
lines.note: the day's object from the other side: refused now, not later. Pairs with the NYT 10-21 report (plans for after the midterms) — the same window from two papers
lines.zWhy: a proposal refused on timing is the next strike deferred, not denied

lines.quote: without Trump, no GBU-57s — the 30,000-pound bunker-busters B-2s dropped on Fordow and Natanz in June 2025
lines.note: the one instrument Israel cannot supply itself, named and dated
lines.zWhy: the deep sites unreachable without Washington is the objective unreachable alone

lines.quote: if Israel attacked without US support, Iran might retaliate on Israeli territory and avoid US targets and disruption to the Strait of Hormuz
lines.note: H6 touched: the Strait as Iran's instrument, withheld by choice. Marked: this line reads H6. A reader's hypothesis, not the record
lines.zWhy: a strait Iran chooses not to close is a strait Iran controls

lines.quote: Israel is already widely shunned over its genocide in Gaza; this could isolate it further
lines.note: the masthead's own verdict word, unattributed — the page's one denominated line. Non-US horizon: the word is the publication's register, flagged, not scored as a US reading
lines.zWhy: isolation named is a cost the next strike adds

lines.quote: you cannot change a regime unless you deploy troops and stay for some years; Israel cannot control Iran, and the US would not undertake another — decades
lines.note: THE CLOSE: the falsifier the principal set in March, returned by the analyst as the answer. 'Decades' is the page's last number
lines.zWhy: a change priced in decades that no one will buy is no change
